flawed_step: The step from 'no single-vertex move strictly increases the cut' (each vertex has at least as many neighbours across as on its own side) to 'the cut value is maximum' cannot be justified. Local optimality only excludes single-vertex moves, not moving several vertices at once.
counterexample: C6 with vertices 1..6 and partition {1,2,4,5} | {3,6}: the cut edges are 23, 34, 56, 61, so the cut value is 4. Vertices 1, 2, 4, 5 each have one neighbour on each side, so moving one leaves the value unchanged; vertices 3 and 6 have both neighbours across, so moving one lowers it. No single move improves the cut, yet the bipartition {1,3,5} | {2,4,6} has cut value 6.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. A partition that cannot be improved by a single-vertex move only guarantees that each vertex has at least half its neighbours across, not a global maximum. In the 6-cycle, the partition {1,2,4,5} | {3,6} cannot be improved by moving one vertex but has cut value 4, while the maximum cut is 6.
